name: When do I need a general contractor instead of hiring individual trade specialists?

mainEntity.name: When do I need a general contractor instead of hiring individual trade specialists?

acceptedAnswer.text: You generally need a general contractor whenever a project involves multiple trades, structural changes, or coordinated rough-ins alongside finish work. For example, moving a shower or adding a basement bathroom involves framing, drywall, waterproofing, tile setting, plumbing, and electrical. A general contractor serves as a single point of contact to supervise the site, organize specialized sub-trades, and complete finish carpentry directly. If your project is strictly a single minor task, like patching a small drywall hole or painting a bedroom, a straightforward handyman visit usually suffices.
acceptedAnswer.description: Hire a general contractor when your remodel involves multiple trades, layout changes, or custom framing so one lead contact manages the schedule and quality.
